name: High1 Korea - Snow Week
summary: Eight days built around High1 Resort in Jeongseon, Gangwon-do — picked over Yongpyong (bigger but icier and skier-oriented), Phoenix Pyeongchang (better Olympic slopestyle park, weaker everything else) and Vivaldi (night-party hill, short runs) because High1 is the strongest all-round snowboard hill in Korea: the country's best natural snow quality at the highest base (733 m to 1,376 m), 18 trails with genuine top-to-bottom fall lines, and lift lines that stay near zero even on weekends per repeated rider reports. Five ride days including two verified night sessions (official night operation 18:00–01:00), a coal-country rest day (mine-turned-art-museum, 7th-century Jeokmyeolbogung temple), gondre-bap and hanwoo BBQ nights in the ex-mining towns of Gohan and Sabuk, and Seoul food bookends. Limiters: all lifts pause 16:00–18:00 daily for grooming; posted prices are the official 2023–24 sheet (adult all-day ₩104,000 range — confirm current season); High1 is the farthest major resort from Seoul (~3h40m rail to Gohan Station plus free resort shuttle, or winter-only direct ski bus from Incheon T1); the surrounding towns are casino-economy mining settlements — authentic, cheap, and quiet on weeknights. Budget posture: local dolsot gukbap and station-front grills over resort food courts, time-based lift tickets over all-day passes when legs fade.

activities.name: Gwangjang Market arrival food crawl
activities.description: Land, drop bags, and eat: lard-griddled bindaetteok (₩4,000–5,000 a pancake), mayak gimbap dipped in mustard-soy, and yukhoe in Seoul's oldest surviving market. Caveat: the general market stalls wind down around 18:00 — it's the food alley, running to roughly 23:00, that you're here for, so come hungry rather than to shop.

activities.name: Mugunghwa rail into the Taebaek mountains
activities.description: Board a Mugunghwa-ho at Cheongnyangni Station and climb through river gorges and old coal valleys to Gohan Station, where High1's free shuttle meets the line — the slow-rail approach is half the trip. Caveat: High1's official directions quote about 3h40m but only a handful of departures run daily — book the exact train on Korail (1544-7788) before travel day.

activities.name: First afternoon laps on High1
activities.description: Shake off travel legs with a 3-hour time ticket (adult ₩58,000 on the official 2023–24 sheet) and lap the wide groomers off the gondolas to learn the mountain's three zones before the big days. Caveat: hourly-ticket time starts counting from your first gate scan, not purchase — don't scan in until you're strapped and ready.

activities.name: Gondre-bap dinner on Gohan's station-front strip
activities.description: Skip the resort food court for Gohan town's local strip: Memilchon Makguksu near the station serves stone-pot gondre (thistle) rice and buckwheat makguksu from patented house recipes, with gondre set meals around ₩15,000 at neighbors like Hambaeksan Dolsotbap. Caveat: peak-season waits of 30+ minutes are commonly reported at the area's gondre spots at lunch — dinner is the calmer slot.

activities.name: Full ride day 1 — top-to-bottom fall lines
activities.description: Ride the official daytime session gate-to-gate: 18 trails off a 1,376 m summit with the best variety of true top-to-bottom runs at any single Korean resort, on snow riders consistently rate the country's cleanest. Caveat: all lifts stop for the daily grooming window 16:00–18:00 — day session ends hard at 16:00, so front-load your laps.

activities.name: High1 Top sauna soak
activities.description: Boil the ride day out of your legs Korean-style at High1 Top, the sauna on the 4th floor of the Grand Hotel Convention Tower (06:00–22:00, adult ₩28,000). Caveat: it stays closed until 14:00 every Monday — shift sauna night if your rest day lands wrong.

activities.name: Full ride day 2 — zones and tree lines
activities.description: Work the mountain's far zones and steeper Victoria-side pitches; weekday lift lines here are famously near-nonexistent, so lap counts run high even on a time ticket. Caveat: time tickets aren't sold during the 16:00–18:00 maintenance window, and if the window overlaps your ticket the usable time extends by 2 hours — plan purchases around it.

activities.name: Night session under the lights
activities.description: Korea's signature riding hours: High1's official night operation runs 18:00–01:00, with freshly groomed corduroy the moment gates reopen after the two-hour reset. Caveat: 18:00–01:00 is the official session window, but which slopes stay lit varies with conditions — check the day's operations board before buying the night ticket.

activities.name: Samtan Art Mine — rest-day coal-to-art complex
activities.description: Korea's first 'art mine': the Samcheok Tanjwa colliery, worked for 40 years, reborn as galleries and preserved washrooms and winding-gear halls holding 100,000+ works from some 150 countries (admission ₩10,000–13,000). Caveat: closed every Monday, and winter weekday hours are only 10:00–17:00 (weekends 09:30–17:30) — call +82-33-591-3001 before heading up the valley.

activities.name: Jeongamsa Temple and the Sumano Pagoda
activities.description: One of Korea's five Jeokmyeolbogung temples, founded by master Jajang in the 7th century to enshrine relics of the Buddha, with the Goryeo-era brick-stone Sumano Pagoda up a ten-minute forest path behind the main hall. Caveat: winter footing on the pagoda path isn't documented — confirm conditions ahead and wear real boots, not resort slides.

activities.name: Hanwoo BBQ and soju night in Sabuk
activities.description: Grill night in the old mining town below the resort: Donnara Unara near Sabuk Station does premium hanwoo beef and pork over charcoal, with the town's casual pubs for a soju nightcap after. Caveat: hanwoo is priced as the premium it is and the restaurant's exact hours aren't published in English — confirm ahead and let the pork shoulder carry the budget.

activities.name: Full ride day 3 — powder-morning patrol
activities.description: Chase whatever fell overnight — High1's altitude keeps snow drier than anywhere else in Korea, and rested legs from the off-day are for the steepest lines on the hill. Caveat: the posted fee sheet (adult all-day ₩100,000, 3h ₩58,000) is the official 2023–24 season table — verify current-season pricing at the ticket office or high1.com before budgeting the week.

activities.name: Kangwon Land casino look-in
activities.description: A one-of-a-kind Korean institution next to the slopes: the only casino in the country that Korean nationals may legally enter, built to revive these coal towns, with a foreigner-only gaming zone added in February 2025 and free admission for foreign passport holders (19+). Caveat: entry requires your physical passport — a driver's license is explicitly not accepted, so carry it from the hotel.

activities.name: Final ride day — victory laps
activities.description: Last daytime session: repeat the week's best top-to-bottom lines and bank the legs you need for the farewell night ride. Caveat: if you're saving energy, the time-based tickets (3/5/7/9-hour tiers from ₩58,000, clock starting at first gate scan) beat the all-day pass — decide at the gate, not the night before.

activities.name: Farewell night session
activities.description: Close the week the Korean way — empty corduroy under floodlights on the official 18:00–01:00 night session, then pack for the morning train back to Cheongnyangni and the airport run. Caveat: gates open exactly at 18:00 after the fixed 16:00–18:00 grooming shutdown — arriving at 17:00 buys you nothing but cold toes.

pois.name: High1 Resort slopes
pois.description: 18 trails and 9 lifts (3 gondolas) between 733 m and a 1,376 m summit above the old coal towns of Sabuk and Gohan — Korea's highest-quality natural snow and its best single-resort variety of top-to-bottom runs, opened 2006 under public corporation Kangwon Land.

pois.name: High1 Resort base (Valley area)
pois.description: Main base area with ticket gates, rental halls and gondola loading; time-based lift tickets (3/5/7/9-hour and all-day) are the house system, with daytime 09:00–16:00 and night 18:00–01:00 sessions.

pois.name: High1 Top sauna (Grand Hotel Convention Tower 4F)
pois.description: Resort sauna and baths on the Grand Hotel Convention Tower's 4th floor; 06:00–22:00, adult ₩28,000, closed until 14:00 on Mondays.

pois.name: Kangwon Land Casino
pois.description: The only casino in South Korea open to Korean nationals, created to revitalize the coal-mining valley; foreigners enter free with a passport (19+), and a foreigner-only gaming zone opened on the 5th floor in February 2025.

pois.name: Gwangjang Market
pois.description: Seoul's century-old covered market whose food alley — bindaetteok griddles, mayak gimbap counters, yukhoe stalls — runs into the late evening while the textile stalls close around 18:00.

pois.name: Gohan station-front eat street
pois.description: The cluster of local restaurants around Gohan Station and its main street — Memilchon Makguksu (patented gondre-bap and buckwheat makguksu), Hambaeksan Dolsotbap (gondre stone-pot set ~₩15,000 with a spread of banchan) and casual grills — the authentic alternative to resort food courts.

pois.name: Sabuk station-front dining strip (Donnara Unara)
pois.description: Sabuk-eup's compact restaurant strip near the station, a short shuttle or taxi below the resort; Donnara Unara anchors it with premium hanwoo and pork charcoal BBQ, flanked by fried-chicken joints and local pubs.

pois.name: Samtan Art Mine
pois.description: Former Samcheok Tanjwa coal mine turned art complex (opened 2013) preserving winding towers, miners' washrooms and coal infrastructure alongside 100,000+ artworks; winter weekdays 10:00–17:00, weekends 09:30–17:30, closed Mondays, admission ₩10,000–13,000.

pois.name: Jeongamsa Temple & Sumano Pagoda
pois.description: 7th-century Jeokmyeolbogung temple founded by master Jajang to enshrine relics of the Buddha — one of only five such temples in Korea — with the Goryeo-era Sumano brick-stone pagoda a ten-minute climb behind the main hall.

transit.name: Incheon International Airport Terminal 1
transit.description: Arrival/departure hub; AREX trains connect to Seoul for the bookend days, and the winter-only High1 Ski Bus departs direct from the T1 1st-floor 1C stop (~4h, reservation via kdtour.rideus.net, +82-2-335-5889).

transit.name: Cheongnyangni Station (Seoul)
transit.description: Seoul railhead for the Taebaek Line: Mugunghwa-ho trains to Gohan take about 3h40m per High1's official directions — book seats on Korail (1544-7788), departures are limited.

transit.name: Gohan Station
transit.description: Closest rail stop to High1; the resort runs a free pick-up shuttle from the station, and the town's eat street is directly out front.

transit.name: Sabuk Station
transit.description: One stop before Gohan and closest to Sabuk town's BBQ strip and intercity bus terminal (Dong Seoul buses ~2h40m); taxis and resort shuttles link it to the base area.
